title: The vault and the mint wallet
takeaway: Mint from a fresh wallet with only what you need, and keep your dragons in a vault that never connects to new sites.

cards.title: One wallet for everything
cards.body: Keeper Aro keeps every NFT, all his ETH and his game tokens in one wallet. He connects it to every new site he finds. Today a site offers a free egg to early Keepers. One wrong click here could put everything he owns at risk at once.

url.label: Secure prefix
url.why: https only means encrypted, not honest.

url.label: Unknown free egg site
url.why: A new site you have never checked.

page.title: Free egg for early Keepers
lines: Connect the wallet that holds your dragons.

cards.title: Two wallets, two jobs
cards.body: A hot wallet lives in an app or browser and touches new sites. A vault, or cold wallet, holds what you keep and never connects to new sites. For mint, use a fresh wallet with only the price plus gas. After mint, send your dragon to the vault.
points: A bad click in the mint wallet cannot reach the vault.

cards.title: A hardware wallet is not a shield
cards.body: A hardware wallet keeps your keys off the internet, which stops key theft. It does not stop a request you approve. If you confirm a bad approval, a scammer can take your tokens without ever touching your keys. Read what the device screen says, every time, before you press confirm.

cards.title: Lock the accounts around you
cards.body: Scammers also take over the accounts around your wallet. In a SIM swap, a scammer gets your phone number moved to their own SIM card and then receives your text codes. For email, X and Discord, use an authenticator app or a security key instead of text message codes.
points: Start with email: it can reset your other accounts.

questions.stem: Presale opens soon. Which wallet should you mint from?
options: A fresh wallet holding only price and gas
Your vault, so the dragon lands safely there
Your main wallet, so the history looks trusted
A hardware wallet holding all your other NFTs
questions.why: A fresh mint wallet with a small balance limits what one bad click can reach. Your vault stays away from new sites.

questions.stem: You use a hardware wallet. A site asks you to approve all your NFTs. Are you protected?
options: No, approving still gives the spender access
Yes, hardware wallets block bad approvals
Yes, as long as it is plugged in
Yes, because the keys never leave it
questions.why: With an approval, nobody needs your keys to take your tokens. A hardware wallet gives no extra protection against what you approve.

seg.t: Keep everything in one wallet, it is simpler.

seg.why: One bad click could then reach everything.

seg.t: Write your seed phrase on paper.
seg.label: Paper backup
seg.why: Good advice: paper kept offline cannot be scanned.

seg.t: With a hardware wallet you can sign anything.
seg.label: Sign anything
seg.why: A device cannot stop a request you approve.

questions.why: Split the jobs: a small mint wallet for new sites, a vault that never connects. A hardware wallet still signs whatever you confirm.

questions.stem: A scammer calls your phone company pretending to be you. What could they take?
options: Your number, and the text codes sent to it
Your seed phrase, since it is saved on the SIM
Your NFTs, straight from the wallet app
Nothing, since your wallet is not linked
questions.why: In a SIM swap your number moves to their SIM, so text codes go to them. An authenticator app or security key avoids this.

questions.stem: You want to try a new game site that asks to connect. Which wallet do you use?
options: Your mint wallet with a small balance
Your vault, since it is the safest
The wallet with the most ETH
Any, connecting is always the same
questions.why: New sites meet only the small hot wallet. Your vault never connects to new sites, so a bad request there cannot reach your dragons.

questions.stem: You are setting up two step login on your email before mint. Which choice protects best against a SIM swap?
options: An authenticator app or a security key
Text message codes to your phone number
A longer password plus text message codes
Email codes sent to a backup address
questions.why: Text codes follow your phone number, which a SIM swap can steal. The FTC advises an authentication app or a security key.

questions.why: A hardware wallet confirms whatever you approve. An unknown site asking your vault to approve all NFTs is a reject.

questions.stem: After mint, your dragon sits in your mint wallet. What is the best next step?
options: Send it to your vault, checking the address
Leave it and keep using that wallet everywhere
Keep it there, the mint wallet is fresh
Connect the vault to the mint site
questions.why: Moving the dragon to your vault keeps it away from new sites. Copy the vault address from your own wallet and check it.

questions.why: Gifts that need your vault to connect are a lure. Keep the vault offline and check gift news in the official channels.

questions.stem: A post says holders must connect their vault to claim a holder gift. What do you do?
options: Keep the vault offline and check official channels
Connect it once, gifts are rare
Connect through the hardware wallet, so it is fine
Move everything to the mint wallet first
questions.why: The vault rule has no gift exception. Check the news on the official accounts yourself before you connect anything.
